ARCHITECTURE

The system behind every payment.

AUTRA separates intelligence from financial control. The agent decides what it wants to do; AUTRA checks the rules before value moves.

From AI intent to settlement

Every transaction passes through a clear set of layers. This makes autonomous payments programmable instead of giving an agent a completely open wallet.

01AI AgentCreates a payment request.
02AUTRA SDK / APIReceives and formats the request.
03Wallet + Policy EngineChecks balance, limits and permissions.
04Identity + RiskChecks the agent and recipient.
05AUTRA L2Executes the network transaction.
06Stablecoin SettlementValue reaches the approved recipient.

THE PROBLEM

AI can act. Money is still the missing layer.

AI agents can already call APIs, search data, use compute and execute workflows. The difficult part is letting them handle money safely. Traditional wallets are made for humans, while autonomous software needs permissions, limits, identity and machine-readable settlement.

Unlimited Access

Giving an agent a normal wallet can mean giving it more financial power than it actually needs.

Too Many Approvals

Humans should not have to manually approve every small payment made by software.

No Native Reputation

A wallet address does not explain whether an agent is reliable, active or risky.

Fragmented Commerce

Agents need a common way to discover services and settle payments with other software.

ARCHITECTURE

The financial layer under the agent.

AUTRA is designed as an application and protocol layer on an L2. The goal is to keep payments cheap and fast while putting policy, identity and agent logic above settlement.

System Stack

AI AgentResearch, trading, support, data or other autonomous software.
↓
AUTRA SDK / APISimple interface developers use to create wallets, policies and payments.
↓
Policy + Identity LayerChecks budgets, permissions, approved recipients and agent identity.
↓
AUTRA L2High-frequency, low-cost transaction execution and settlement.
↓
Stablecoin SettlementStablecoins such as USDC/USDT can carry the actual payment value.

What each layer does

Agent LayerThe AI decides what task it needs to complete.
Wallet LayerThe agent gets a dedicated programmable financial account.
Policy LayerRules decide what the agent is allowed to do before funds move.
Identity & ReputationActivity builds a persistent record that can help other agents assess trust.
Settlement LayerThe approved payment is executed and recorded on the network.
Why an L2?

Machine payments can happen frequently. An L2 is intended to reduce transaction cost and latency compared with putting every small agent payment directly on a base layer.

TRANSACTION FLOW

One payment, eight simple checks.

Example: a research agent needs a $3 data service. AUTRA turns that request into a controlled financial action instead of an unrestricted wallet transaction.

Request

Agent submits a payment request for an approved service.

Identity

AUTRA verifies the agent and its assigned wallet.

Policy

Budget, per-payment limits and permissions are evaluated.

Recipient

The destination is checked against approved services.

Risk

Unusual activity can be paused or escalated when necessary.

Approval

Higher-risk actions can be routed to a human operator.

Settlement

Approved value settles in stablecoins on the network.

Record

The transaction updates activity and reputation signals.

REVENUE MODEL

A network that can earn from usage.

The business model is designed around real product usage rather than forcing the native token to be the payment currency. Stablecoins can handle settlement while AUTRA monetizes infrastructure and services.

01
Network / Service Fee

A small fee can be charged on eligible transactions or premium settlement services.

02
Developer Infrastructure

Businesses can pay for higher limits, advanced APIs, analytics, monitoring and enterprise tooling.

03
Agent Marketplace

AUTRA can take a defined fee when agents discover and purchase third-party services through the marketplace.

04
Enterprise Controls

Teams can pay for managed policies, fleet management, reporting and compliance-oriented infrastructure.

Simple example

If a future production network processed $1,000,000 of eligible monthly volume and the effective infrastructure fee averaged 20%:

$1,000,000 × 0.20% = $2,000

This is only an illustrative example — the final fee model, exclusions and revenue split would be defined before launch.

Important principle

Payments can stay denominated in stablecoins. $AUTRA does not need to be artificially inserted into every payment just to create utility.

SECURITY & CONTROL

Autonomy without giving up control.

The core product should assume that agents can make mistakes. AUTRA is designed around permissions and containment so a single agent cannot automatically access everything.

Spending Limits

Per-transaction, daily and periodic budgets limit the amount an agent can move.

Recipient Allowlists

Funds can be restricted to approved contracts, services or addresses.

Human Escalation

Large, unusual or sensitive actions can require a human approval step.

Monitoring

Transaction behaviour can be watched for unusual patterns and risk signals.

Emergency Controls

Admin or governance-defined pause and recovery mechanisms can limit damage during incidents.

Audits

Smart contracts and critical infrastructure should go through independent security review before production.

DEVELOPER LAYER

Build once. Let agents transact.

Developers should not need to build wallets, spending policies and settlement infrastructure from scratch. AUTRA exposes these capabilities through a simple integration layer.

Create Agent

Register an agent and attach a persistent identity.

Create Wallet

Generate a dedicated wallet with programmable permissions.

Set Policy

Define budgets, recipients and approval conditions.

Example integration flow

createAgent() ↓ createWallet() ↓ setPolicy({ dailyLimit, txLimit, allowlist }) ↓ fundWallet(USDC) ↓ pay(service, amount) ↓ policyCheck → riskCheck → settlement ↓ transactionConfirmed()
The above is a product-flow illustration, not a final production SDK. The actual API, smart contracts and developer tooling would be specified during protocol development.

SECURITY & CONTROL

Autonomous does not mean uncontrolled.

The owner defines the boundaries. AUTRA enforces them at transaction time. Larger or unusual actions can be routed back to a human.

Spending Limits

Set per-payment, daily and recurring budgets for every agent.

Allowlisted Recipients

Restrict where an agent is allowed to send funds.

Human Escalation

Require approval when a transaction crosses a defined threshold.

Monitoring & Audits

Track behaviour and plan independent contract/security reviews before production.
